  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2019  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 5, 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT — OCTOBER 2019

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of October 2019.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 655 –
  ADOPTION OF THE 2019 CALIFORNIA BUILDING AND FIRE CODES

  The California Building Standards Commission has adopted new building and
  fire codes to take effect on January 1, 2020. Publications were available as of
  July of this year. The Building and Safety Division and Fire Department staff
  have monitored the development of these codes closely, and are engaging in
  training to ensure that the City’s building and safety and fire personnel are
  properly trained to implement the new standards.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 655.

  E. SENATE BILL 2 (SB 2) PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM RESOLUTION NO.
  19-57

  Senate Bill 2 (SB 2) Planning Grants provide funding and technical assistance
  to all local governments in California to help Cities and counties prepare,
  adopt, and implement plans and process improvements that streamline
  housing approvals and accelerate housing production. The City is currently in
  the process of completing an application requesting for funds.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2019  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-57.
  Authorizing application for, and receipt of; SB 2 Planning Grants Program
  Funds.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 19-55 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT 400
  WEST BROADWAY BETWEEN SANTA ANITA STREET AND JUNIPERO
  PLACE ON FEBRUARY 7, 2020

  The Public Works Department received a request from San Gabriel Mission
  High School for a temporary street closure for a walk-a-thon carnival. The
  requested date and time of the closure is Friday, February 7, 2020 from 7:30
  a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on Broadway between Santa Anita Street and Junipero Place.
  Activities for this event will be held on the school’s private property. The street
  closure will enable participants to walk safely back and forth from the campus
  on the south side of Broadway to the school’s field on the north side of
  Broadway. Access to nearby properties will not be affected by this closure.
  Therefore, the Neighbor Consent Form is not required. Resolution No. 19-55
  details the location, date and times for the closure, as well the conditions that
  must be followed by the applicant. The Public Works Department, Fire
  Department and Police Department have reviewed and approved the request.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-55
  authorizing closure of Broadway between Santa Anita Street and Junipero
  Place from 7:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on Friday, February 7, 2020.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CITY OF SAN GABRIEL ANALYSIS OF PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES

  As directed by the City Council, a review of the City’s current parking
  enforcement contract model versus the possibility of establishing its’ own ‘in
  house’ program has been conducted with the following report offered as its
  findings. The City of San Gabriel has contracted with InterCon Security for
  parking enforcement services since November 2015. The term of the current
  contract is three (3) years beginning September 1, 2018 and ending June 30,
  2021. The initial term of the agreement was for one year (September 2018 to
  June 2019) with two (2) option periods of one year each and each party (City

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2019  4
   and InterCon) has the right to terminate the agreement without cause with
  sixty days’ advance written notice.

  Recommended Action:

  Based on staff’s analysis of cost, workers’ compensation, unemployment, and
  general liability exposure, down time due to potential staff shortage and
  required recruitment/training time for replacements, required expanded
  program supervision, and initial start-up costs, it does not seem fiscally
  practical to establish an “in-house” parking enforcement program. Therefore,
  staff recommends continuing the current model of contract services for
  parking enforcement efforts.

  B. LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT FEASIBILITY STUDY

  In 2016, the San Gabriel Fire Department commissioned a Standards of Cover
  Survey (SOC Survey) to study its service delivery model and make
  recommendations for future operations. One recommendation from the
  report was to explore consolidation of the Fire Department into the
  Consolidated Fire Protection District of Los Angeles County (LA County Fire
  Department). On May 15, 2018, the San Gabriel City Council requested a
  Feasibility Study and on January 15, 2019, Council authorized a Conversion
  Cost Study with the Los Angeles County Fire Department. The Operational
  Overview and Financial Analysis of these studies, immediate and future needs
  of the current Department and service delivery enhancements are presented
  in this report for consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council defer a decision on annexation of the
  Fire Department into the Consolidated Fire Protection District of Los Angeles
  County until after the results of the sales tax measure are known when there
  is a clearer understanding of the City’s financial picture.

MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 19, 2019
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Pu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:33 p.m.
  on Tuesday, November 19, 2019, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Liao.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Juli Costanzo, John R. Harrington, Chin Ho Liao, Vice
  Mayor Denise Menchaca, and Mayor Jason Pu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto; City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux;  Assistant  City  Manager/Community

I  Development Director Armine Chaparyan; Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Ch ief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck; Interim Fire Chief Steven Wallace;
  Management Specialist/Acting Finance Director Paula
  Chamberlain, Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Council Member Liao, seconded by Council Member
  Harrington, to approve the agenda order. Hearing no objection, Mayor Pu announced
  that the agenda order was approved.
  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. CALIFORNIA HIGHWAY PATROL AUTO THEFT RECOGNITION

I  Presentation was made by Police Captain Fabian Valdez.

  B. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT VIDEO

  Presentation was made by Police Chief Eugene Harris.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Rae Huang submitted a speaker's request card but was not present to speak.

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  November 19, 2019
   The following speakers requested that the City Council enact a moratorium on no-
  fault evictions prior to new legislation enacting the same that goes into effect January
  1, 2020: Teresa Eilers, United Way of Greater Los Angeles; Sean McMorris, resident,
  who also submitted a written comment; Eric Sunada; and Paul Padilla, resident.

  Chi Chang expressed dissatisfaction with his experience protesting a parking violation.

  Mayor Pu noted for those advocating during public comment for the no-fault eviction

I  moratorium that the matter will be addressed during Council comments.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Pu noted a correction to the Minutes of the November 5, 2019 Regular Meeting
  that the approval of the agenda order was motioned by Council Member Harrington
  and seconded by Council Member Liao. He requested that detail be added regarding
  questions asked by Council Member Liao related to item 4E, along with the motion,
  second, and vote for that item.

  A motion was made by Council Member Liao, seconded by Vice Mayor Menchaca, to
  approve Consent Calendar item 4A as amended and items 4B - 4F as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar items 4A as amended and 48 - 4F as presented by
  a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  COSTANZO, HARRINGTON, LIAO, MENCHACA, PU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

I  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  City Council approved the following :

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 5, 2019.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  City Council approved the October 25, 2019, and November 1, 2019, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT- OCTOBER 2019

  City Council approved the Cash and Investment Report - October 2019.

  D. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 655 -ADOPTION OF
  THE 2019 CALIFORNIA BUILDING AND FIRE CODES

I  City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 655.

  E. SENATE BILL 2 (SB 2) PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM RESOLUTION NO. 19-
  57

  City Council adopted Resolution No. 19-57 authorizing application for, and
  receipt of, SB 2 Planning Grants Program Funds.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  November 19, 2019
   F. RESOLUTION NO. 19-55 FOR TEMPORARY STREET CLOSURE AT 400 WEST
  BROADWAY BETWEEN SANTA ANITA STREET AND JUNIPERO PLACE ON
  FEBRUARY 7, 2020

  City Council adopted Resolution No. 19-55 authorizing closure of Broadway
  between Santa Anita Street and Junipero Place from 7:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on
  Friday, February 7, 2020.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

I  6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CITY OF SAN GABRIEL ANALYSIS OF PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES

  Presentation was made by Police Captain Fabian Valdez.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included parking violation revenue amount variations from year to year;
  yearly increases for contract services with lnterCon; parking enforcement in-house
  versus by contract; factors that determine revenue amounts; non-response to the
  City's Request for Proposals (RFP); the basis for vendor fee increases and year-to-
  year variations; and parking enforcement models used by other cities.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to receive and file the report and to
  revisit the item in June 2020.

I
  B. LOS ANGELES COUNTY FIRE DEPARTMENT FEASIBILITY STUDY

  Presentation was made by Interim Fire Chief Wallace and Management
  Specialist/Acting Finance Director Chamberlain.

  Mayor Pu opened the public comment period.

  Helen Yuan, resident, and Carina Rivera, resident, spoke in favor of conversion to
  Los Angeles County for fire services.

  Kirk Goltermann, President of the San Gabriel Firefighters Association (FFA), spoke
  in favor of conversion to Los Angeles County for fire services on behalf of himself
  and the following FFA Members who were also present: Antonio Negrete, John
  Adkins, Philip Apparis, Hrag Jivalegian, Cuong Tran, Chris Backley, Jacob Gustafson,
  Michael Rebolledo, Greg Kernodle, and Sean Irwin.

  Sally Baldwin, resident, commended the good service she has received from the
  San Gabriel Fire Department and its community involvement, expressed concern
  about what response time would be with the Los Angeles County Fire Department,

I  and stated she wants the best for the San Gabriel Fire Department and the City.

  Discussion included a comparison of San Gabriel Fire Department (SGFD) and Los
  Angeles County Fire Department (LACFD) service models relative to position titles
  and duties, Advanced Life Saving (ALS) and Basic Life Saving (BLS) services, mutual
  aid, response time, equipment capabilities related to larger and higher
  development projects, community engagement, and financial impacts related to
  retirement unfunded liability; development fees to support Fire Department
  equipment needs; auto-aid agreements and LACFD response relative to regional
  emergencies; the City's Fire Station repair obligations under a County service

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  November 19, 2019
   model; contractual guarantees on what costs the County could and could not pass
  on to the City; fee caps and roll -overs; and property tax distribution to County Fire
  District cities versus contract cities.

  Discussion continued on means of ensuring payment under the County model; the
  City's use of mutual aid being consistent with similarly-sized cities; the Los Angeles
  County Emergency Medical Services Agency yearly audit on the SGFD paramedic
  program which found SGFD is doing very well; stakeholder and community
  outreach regarding the consideration of conversion to LACFD; personnel transfer

I  subsequent to conversion; SGFD has no outstanding environmental hazard
  abatement issues; restrictions on the use of retirement tax funds; and concern
  about hidden costs and increases that cannot be negotiated under a County
  contract.

  Following additional discussion on financial considerations and a five -year
  strategic plan the SGFD is preparing relative to the option of keeping fire services
  in-house, a motion was made by Council Member Harrington, seconded by Council
  Member Costanzo to receive and file the report and to defer a decision on
  annexation of the Fire Department into the Consolidated Fire Protection District of
  Los Angeles County until after the results of the sales tax measure are known when
  there is a clearer understanding of the City's financial picture.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  COSTANZO, HARRINGTON, LIAO, MENCHACA, PU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Li'i Furumoto of Asian Americans Advancing Justice - Los Angeles spoke in favor of
  the City enacting a moratorium on no-fault evictions prior to new legislation enacting the
  same that goes into effect January 1, 2020

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT - None.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Mayor Pu requested that the City Council schedule a special meeting to consider an
  urgency ordinance placing a moratorium on evictions as advocated for by numerous
  public speakers at tonight's meeting. There was a consensus of the City Council to
  schedule the special meeting for November 21 , 2019, at 7:00 a.m.

  Mayor Pu reported that the City was a finalist for the Eddy awards but did not win, and
  commended and thanked staff for their efforts. He announced that meetings for the
  Lunar New Year event have begun, reported that he will be attending the San Gabriel

I  Valley Council of Governments (COG) Transportation and General Board meetings on
  November 21 , 2019, and commented that the Elections Investigation Report from
  2013 had been located and redacted, and is available for review.

  Council Member Harrington thanked staff and participants for a well -attended Turkey
  Trot event; wished everyone a happy and safe Thanksgiving; reminded the community
  of the Tree-Lighting in Plaza Park on December 3, 2019, at 6:00 p.m.; and requested
  that staff prepare an analysis of changes to Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)
  requirements pursuant to AB-68.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  November 19, 2019
   Vice Mayor Menchaca requested an update on the timeline for the sales tax measure
  informational campaign, and reported that she had written a letter of
  recommendation as Vice Mayor relative to the Strategic, Tactical, Resilient Interdiction
  of Violent Extremism (STRIVE) conference she previously reported on.

  Council Member Costanzo commented on a great Turkey Trot event and that is was
  great to see everyone at the meeting tonight.

I  Council Member Liao reported on his attendance at a seminar put on by the Minority
  Business Development Agency and Small Business Administration on how to survive
  natural disasters, and the Soroptimist Live Your Dream Award event at the Sheraton.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  Mayor Pu recessed the meeting at 9:54 p.m. and reconvened into closed session at 10:05
  p.m.

  10. CLOSED SESSION

  A. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION(§ 54957)
  Title: City Manager

  There was no reportable action.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Pu adjourned the meeting at 10:38 p.m.
